q: The legacy loop increments `turns_taken` inside an `async_stream::try_stream!`. Why not a plain `for turn in 0..max` loop?
options: The loop must yield live stream items mid-iteration (UI token streaming); a plain loop cannot emit without buffering
A plain loop would compile but panic at runtime
Rust forbids for loops inside async functions
The team prefers while loops for style reasons
explanation: Plain loops compile fine here; the constraint is yielding, not crashing.
for loops are legal in async fn bodies.
The choice is architectural (streaming), not stylistic.

q: In the legacy loop, what happens to a tool request when goose_mode is Chat?
options: A synthetic skip response is appended (CHAT_MODE_TOOL_SKIPPED_RESPONSE) so the model sees the call was not executed
The loop panics
The request is silently dropped with no response
Goose switches to Approve mode automatically
explanation: Chat mode is a supported path; no panic occurs.
The skip is always answered — otherwise the model can't correct course.
Mode changes require user action via update_goose_mode.

q: Fix this compile error in the loop: `error[E0599]: no method named "resume" found for struct "Agent"`. The method exists on the provider handle instead. Which change unblocks it?
options: Call `self.provider().await?.resume(saved_provider_session_id).await` instead of `self.resume(...)`
Add `unsafe` before the call
Move the call outside the async_stream
Implement resume on Agent by delegating to the UI
explanation: unsafe never adds missing methods; it only permits danger.
The call is already inside an async context; placement is not the issue.
resume is a provider-session concept (picking up a prior upstream session), not a UI concern.
